points.why: It explains that each department's local target (batching, full scanners, block discharge, door-to-doctor) is met by adding delay downstream, so all hit their targets while ED length of stay worsens.
It says the audit would find every department performing and miss the connecting structure, but never says fixing one part in isolation may just move the queue elsewhere.
It recommends tracing patients end to end, splitting waiting time by handoff, finding where queues build, and asking why local targets add up to a worse whole.
It recommends adding cross-department flow measures (ED length of stay, decision-to-bed time, turnaround for ED orders) and accepting some loss of local utilization.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects hunting for one underperforming department and warns against blaming the weakest-looking one.
